title: f-research dossier record
description: One provider, one file. The source of truth for every claim in docs/. A document is a view of this record. Validation is structural only: it proves the fields are present and well-formed, not that the numbers are true. Truth is a probe record plus an evidence date.

topic.description: The docs/ topic this record belongs to. A typo here orphans the record.

slug.description: Stable join key between dossier, document and history entry. Lowercase, hyphenated.

provider.description: The name a human uses, as the vendor writes it.

url.description: The page the numbers came from. Not a search result, not an aggregator.

category.description: The shape: object storage, drive, registry, sandbox, subscription, broker.

tier.description: The named plan or service tier this record is priced at: 'free', 'pro', 'build', or the vendor's own label. A provider with two materially different tiers is two records, not one, because their limits differ and a reader acts on one.

free_tier.description: The headline offer AND the unit it is stated in. Never a bare number.

stated.description: The offer verbatim, with its numbers and qualifiers.

unit.description: The unit the offer is denominated in. 'unlimited' is a unit because it is a claim about absence of one.

metered_on.description: What the quota is counted against, when that differs from the unit.

read_on.description: The date this page was read. Required to make the number a dated fact rather than a rumour.

per_object_cap.description: The largest single object. Separate from the total, always: the biggest caps cluster where retention is shortest.

stated.description: The cap as the vendor states it. Prose is accepted; a bare number is not.

bytes.description: The cap in bytes when it is a single hard number; null when it is soft, tiered or unstated.

retention.description: How long bytes survive without a touch. Separate from the cap, always.

stated.description: Verbatim or near-verbatim. 'Until deleted' and 'unknown' are both valid answers.

days.description: Days before automatic loss; null for indefinite, unknown, or activity-based.

egress.description: The terms, plus whether they are metered, capped or free.

terms.description: What the vendor says about traffic out, with the qualifier that binds.

metered.description: True when traffic out has a price or a quota; false when it is neither.

free_allowance.description: The included volume before metering starts.

price_per_tb.description: Marginal price per TB beyond the allowance, in the vendor's currency.

interface.description: How a client reaches it. Programme access is a hard requirement of this client, so an empty list is a failed record.

interface_detail.description: The vendor's own words about access, when the token list loses a qualifier.

endpoint.description: The API endpoint, when there is one. Never a credential.

tooling.description: What actually works against it: rclone backend, CLI, SDK, restic, borg.

chaining.description: How this combines with other services into the client's stack. One sentence is enough; empty is a defect.

limits.description: Each binding constraint named from the vocabulary, with its number and source. The headline is almost never the constraint that decides.

value.description: The number with its unit: '10 concurrent connections', '750 GB/day'.

source.description: The URL or document that establishes it.

limits_note.description: Limit prose that names no vocabulary kind. Kept rather than dropped, and kept separate so the gate can see it is unclassified.

binding.description: The one constraint that fails first at this client's scale, named from the same seven-value vocabulary as limits[].kind. METHODOLOGY.md section 4.3 and the definition of done require it on a record whose rung is measured or documented; the schema keeps it optional so a migrated record can land before its author has decided. A record carrying limits[] and no binding has not decided what breaks first.

binding_note.description: Why that kind and not another, in one sentence, when the reasoning is not obvious from limits[].

identity_cost.description: What registration costs. The binding constraint on almost every large quota.

detail.description: The evidence for the tier, and any second gate such as a card at signup.

country.description: For country-phone and institution: which country or which institution class.

reliability_note.description: One line of technical reliability: bans, throttles, data loss, silent re-encoding. No legal caveat, ever.

confidence.description: The weakest rung among the fields that decide the verdict.

confidence_legacy.description: The seed corpus's own high/medium/low, preserved verbatim when a record was migrated. The two scales are not equivalent; this field keeps the translation auditable.

confidence_note.description: Why this rung, and what would move it up one.

evidence.description: What each source established, not just that it exists.

url.description: The page, or 'probe:<target>' for a measurement we ran.

date.description: The date the claim was read or measured, UTC. A number without one is a rumour.

proved.description: The specific claim this source supports. 'pricing page' proves nothing.

capture.description: The captured page this row quotes, or for a probe: row the stored probe record: sha256 of its text, stored at sources/c/<first two hex>/<hash>.md.gz (a page) or sources/p/<first two hex>/<hash>.json.gz (a probe record). Required for an http row dated 2026-10-28 or later and a probe: row dated 2026-10-30 or later (scripts/rq check, rule C21).

quote.description: The exact span of the captured page that proves the claim; scripts/rq checks it is in the capture.

verdict.description: 'dead' is a finding, not an omission.

verified_at.description: When the record was last confirmed against the live service. Moves only when somebody actually checked.

price_per_tb_month.description: The comparable number, in the currency stated, at the tier named.

stale.description: Computed by scripts/dossier/staleness.py, never written by hand. True when the record is past its class window, its topic window, or its evidence budget, or when verified_at has been moved without the evidence moving with it. A hand-written value is a claim about freshness that the gate will overwrite on its next run.

stale_checked_at.description: The UTC instant staleness.py last evaluated this record. Written only by the script.

probe.description: A probe.py record, embedded or referenced, for any claim at the measured rung.

history.description: Links to the history/ entries that changed this record.

extras.description: Fields migrated from a source that has no canonical home. Nothing is dropped; it is parked here, visibly.

self_hosted.description: true when what the record offers is software, or a node, that the user installs, runs and maintains on a machine (owned, rented or free): a server, a daemon, a node, an operator in the user's own cluster, or a client, app, editor or agent whose free part serves nothing itself. The hosted service such software reaches keeps its own record. A record stays hosted when the vendor runs the service its free unit or price is spent on, even when the user runs a client, an endpoint, a routing daemon or their own application code against it: a hosted allocation (address space, a tunnel-broker or relay account), a hosted control plane whose workers the user deploys, or a cluster the vendor spins up in a cloud account the user rents. A remote-control account for software the user runs, with no capacity of its own, is self-hosted. false records a reviewed hosted offer; absent means hosted. A self-hosted record is the last resort: every list puts it after every hosted record, and no list stars it, ranks it first or recommends it. The field does not change the verdict.
